meeting_header:
Date: 2026-09-04
Time: 10:30 AM - 11:28 AM PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Derek Soto (Redwood), Jordan Lee (Aurora CTO), Maya Patel (Head Infra), Sam Rivera (Lead Data Eng), Ivy Kline (Security)
summary: Decision-day parity review focused on migration from Together/OpenAI/Anthropic to Redwood API. Discussed parity mapping (tokens, streaming, function call, chat state), performance tradeoffs (latency vs cost), security requirements (SOC2, KMS, SAML), and an agreed pilot: 3-day benchmark running Aurora prompts against Redwood Dedicated and Hosted fallbacks. Next: send security pack, schedule perf deep-dive, and start pilot mid-September.
topics: parity mapping, latency SLOs, KV/prefix cache, quantization, streaming & function call compatibility, VPC/private deployment, SOC2/KMS, benchmark plan
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time today. This is the decision day parity review for Aurora migrating off Together/OpenAI. We've got 60 minutes, we'll run through API parity, console, Optimize suggestions, then nail down pilot steps.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Thanks Alex. Big day. We have exec attention, so want to validate there are no major blockers on behaviour parity, and of course latency/cost.
[00:26] Priya Nair: Quick intro - I'm Priya on the Redwood SE team. We'll map the Together and OpenAI endpoints you use to the Redwood API equivalents, call out where there are slight behaviour diffs, and propose mitigations.
[00:39] Maya Patel: Also I'll be watching network and compliance questions. We need VPC, SAML, KMS support and audit trails.
[00:46] Alex Chen: Totally. Ivy from security is on too. Ivy?
[00:50] Ivy Kline: Hi all - brief from security: SOC2 and KMS integration are must haves. We also need proof of data residency controls for EU workloads later.
[00:59] Priya Nair: Ok jumping in. First: request/response parity - for chat, we map Together's chat completions to Redwood's chat endpoint. Function calling: Redwood supports function/tool calling similar to OpenAI's style; payloads and response annotations are slightly different — we include a "tool_invocation" field in the streaming frames rather than in-line metadata, which broke one test in your evals last week.
[01:24] Jordan Lee: That was the edge case where their orchestrator assumed tool calls come at message boundaries. Can you show a sample?
[01:30] Priya Nair: Sure. (shares code link) In practice you can enable the compatibility shim; it normalizes the tool call boundary behaviour. There's negligible overhead.
[01:41] Derek Soto: I want to flag that the shim is a runtime compatibility layer, not a model change; it's opt-in for pilot so we can compare raw outputs too.
[01:49] Sam Rivera: On outputs - our primary worry is subtle tokenization differences leading to scoring changes in downstream NER/classification. How do we guarantee parity?
[01:58] Priya Nair: Two parts. First, tokenization: we surface model tokenizer details and recommend a tokenizer alignment pass in the preprocess. Second, Redwood Optimize will run suggest quantization/batching configs to match latency/cost while preserving output quality; for presubmit we can run a differential eval harness to compute delta F1 across your test set.
[02:20] Jordan Lee: Can you run that eval on our 2k prompt set?
[02:23] Priya Nair: Yes, that's part of the benchmark. We'll run a baseline against your current provider and against the selected Redwood model/quantization profile.
[02:31] Maya Patel: Latency - we're targeting 120ms p50 for short prompts and 400ms p95 for longer interactive flows. Can Redwood hit that on Dedicated?
[02:40] Derek Soto: On Dedicated with appropriate GPU profile and our continuous batching tuned for short-sequence throughput, hitting 120ms p50 is realistic. p95 depends on KV cache hit rate and batching window; we recommend prefix caching for your most common queries to reduce tail latency.
[02:55] Jordan Lee: What's the expected token cost delta? Our CFO is sensitive; Together is low cost for embeddings and chat today.
[03:02] Alex Chen: We'll prepare a cost comparison. Redwood Optimize will produce per-token cost estimates for the chosen quantization, batching, and routing policies. In pilots we usually show 15-40% cost savings versus naive hosted configs depending on cache hit rate.
[03:16] Ivy Kline: Security question - SAML SSO plus SCIM for user provisioning is required. Also audit logs retention 1 year minimum.
[03:25] Priya Nair: Redwood Console supports SAML SSO and SCIM, and audit logs are exportable to S3/Cloud Storage with configurable retention. For Private deployments we support customer KMS/HSM and can be air-gapped.
[03:36] Maya Patel: For pilot we need VPC peering and control plane access. Is Private deployment needed or can we do dedicated with VPC peering?
[03:44] Derek Soto: Dedicated with VPC peering should satisfy pilot. Private deployment is a heavier lift and usually for regulated production. For the benchmark, Dedicated with VPC peering and encrypted in-transit data will be fine.
[03:56] Sam Rivera: On the technical deep dive — I want to understand kernel selection and quantization tradeoffs. We've had degredation when switching to INT8 on some models.
[04:04] Priya Nair: We log perf and quality tradeoffs and recommend mixed precision or 4-bit quant profiles based on evals. We'll run your tests across int8, q4 and q4_0 profiles and surface delta metrics. Our runtime chooses kernels per op; sometimes switching kernels yields quality differences due to fused attention approximations — we'll show exact commits in the deep-dive.
[04:30] Jordan Lee: Any surprises around streaming and partial tokens? Together had slightly different chunking which impacted our websocket client.
[04:38] Derek Soto: Streaming frames are configurable; we can match the chunk size and chunk frequency to mimic your current provider. There might be off-by-one token differences but the client-level API will be compatible.
[04:51] Alex Chen: Let's demo the console quick — show model catalog, rollout controls and the Optimize suggestions.
[04:56] Priya Nair: (screen share) Here is the model catalog. You can pin model variants and set rollout policies; canary traffic split, A/B, automatic fallback to smaller model during overload. For Aurora's traffic spike concerns, a fallback policy is usually set to a cheaper quantized model.
[05:14] Jordan Lee: Can we control routing by region and cost tier?
[05:18] Priya Nair: Yes — smart routing allows rules by latency thresholds, cost budget, or geography. You can set a policy to route EU traffic to eu-region nodes only.
[05:26] Maya Patel: How does KV cache work in multi-tenant Dedicated? We need isolation per customer session.
[05:33] Derek Soto: Cache is tenant-scoped. For Dedicated you get isolated pools. We expose cache metrics in the console so you can see hit-rate per route.
[05:42] Sam Rivera: Benchmark specifics — what's included?
[05:44] Priya Nair: We'll run three baseline runs: (1) current provider default settings, (2) Redwood hosted default model, (3) Redwood Dedicated with Optimize suggested batching/quantization and prefix cache. We'll measure p50/p95 latency, token cost, and output delta metrics (F1/NLL) against your labelled set.
[06:03] Jordan Lee: Ground rule — we need reproducible runs and an agreed seed / deterministic setting for sampling.
[06:09] Priya Nair: We'll use the same sampling seeds and temperature settings you'd been using. Also record the raw logits where possible.
[06:18] Ivy Kline: For compliance we need the benchmark logs and audit trail exported to our S3.
[06:22] Alex Chen: We'll include that in the pilot scoping.
[06:26] Jordan Lee: Any limitations around model size and seq len? We use long context for genomic annotations — sequences up to 8k tokens in some cases.
[06:35] Priya Nair: Redwood supports longer context models; for very long sequences we recommend a chunking + KV cache approach. The runtime supports attention optimization for long contexts; we'll include model recommendations in the report.
[06:49] Derek Soto: Note: longer sequences increase memory and cost; Optimize will trade off chunking size vs latency.
[06:55] Sam Rivera: Can we get a staging environment with limited access for our devs?
[06:59] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll provision a sandbox org with role-based access and SCIM for your dev/test group.
[07:06] Jordan Lee: One last thing — hallucination behavior. We need regression alarms tied to our eval sets.
[07:12] Priya Nair: Redwood offers quality monitors and regression alerts triggered on eval sets. You can configure thresholds (delta F1, hallucination rate) and tie them to rollbacks.
[07:23] Maya Patel: That sounds good. Operationally, our timeline: 2-week pilot then production cutover in 6 weeks assuming success.
[07:30] Alex Chen: For the decision today — are we aligned to run the 3-day benchmark and then reconvene with results?
[07:36] Jordan Lee: Yes, assuming security pack and the VPC details look good.
[07:39] Ivy Kline: We'll need legal review of the pilot contract but security docs first.
[07:44] Alex Chen: Great. Recap of next steps then. Priya, high level of your bench checklist?
[07:48] Priya Nair: We'll produce the runbook: endpoints, sampling seeds, model variants, quantization profiles, and required infra (VPC peering details, peformance counters). Runbook will be shared as a Google Doc and a link to the benchmark harness repo.
[07:59] Sam Rivera: We'll share prompt set and traffic csv by EOW.
[08:02] Alex Chen: Perfect — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the security pack and pilot contract.
[08:06] Jordan Lee: Thank you, look forward to the perf numbers.
[08:09] Derek Soto: I'll schedule the deep dive with your infra team the week after the benchmark.
[08:14] Alex Chen: Closing notes: Pilot start target 2026-09-15, 3-day benchmark, deliverables: security pack, runbook, admin sandbox.
[08:22] (call ends)
questions: How does Redwood handle function/tool calling differences?
Can Dedicated hit 120ms p50 for short prompts?
What quantization profiles preserve quality for our NER tasks?
